values.note: Camping on a Virginia WMA needs a written camping authorization ($10, up to six people) from Go Outdoors Virginia or a license agent, which sets the trip's start and end dates; 14 nights at most. Only in previously cleared spots, and 'unlawful to camp within 300 feet of any lake or facility'. DWR: 'WMA roads are not suitable for long vehicles or trailers ... Some WMAs may not allow travel trailers or RVs.' Briery Creek lists Primitive Camping among its activities; its map marks parking areas but no camping spots.

summary: Confirmed on DWR's Briery Creek page that primitive camping is still allowed, and from DWR's statewide camping page: no hookups, no water/dump/restrooms, 14-night limit, $10 camping authorization. Not stated: season, a camping-specific spot on this WMA. Note left as is (the DWR fee line says what the inherited all-in rate cannot).
flags: Waterfront re-audit lead: entry is lakefront, but DWR's statewide rule (https://dwr.virginia.gov/camping-on-wmas/) says 'It is unlawful to camp within 300 feet of any lake or facility (building, boat ramp, etc.)'. The lakeshore parking areas the note describes sit at boat ramps on Briery Creek Lake, so a legal campsite here cannot be on the water.
